newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Report urges relief agencies to go digital.
newsitem.headline: Report urges relief agencies to go digital.

text.p: Aid agencies are lagging behind in the brave new digital world, where speedy and accurate information on wars and disasters could help save lives and cut costs, an official report said on Wednesday.

Analysis of information is "a skill little known among the humanitarian community and is becoming a key factor in successful fund-raising", the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) report said.
"Despite technological improvements, many decisions are still taken in emergencies with very little information beyond that in people's heads," the IFRC said.
"Vast amounts of information enter and leave organisations without anyone being fully aware of their impact, value or cost."
The IFRC, predicting tougher competition, job cuts and a worsening cash squeeze for aid agencies in the years to come, said relief workers had to revolutionise the way they deal with information.
"Humanitarian aid agencies will have to rethink their traditional role as providers of can-rattling person-to-person aid to become relief information brokers," it said.

In a crisis, aid workers need immediate information about the dispatch of supplies, expert personnel, mapping of conflict zones, locations for refugee camps and local infrastructure such as ports, hospitals and airfields, the Swiss-based IFRC said.
Even rainfall, harvest and livestock price data that could help identify food deficits to help victims of war or disaster should be easily available, the report said.
Agencies must improve coordination in information-management and document reports from previous disasters and conflicts as well as country-specific demographic and geographic data, it added.
Disaster-management information is only slowly becoming available, such as an Internet site used by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) to help trace missing people in Bosnia.
There is also the ReliefWeb, an online international network for the humanitarian community launched by the United Nations Department of Humanitarian Affairs.
